subject: Unexpected p95 jump for model m12q — decision and mitigation logistics
messages:
From: Alyssa Park <alyssa@finmetry.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@finmetry.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: p95 spike on m12q since 03:45 UTC — can you advise?

Hi Priyom,

We started seeing a sustained p95 jump for calls served by model m12q at ~03:45 UTC. Baseline for our app is ~180ms p95; at 03:45 it jumped to ~620ms and has been elevated with occasional spikes to ~900ms. This coincides with the m12q.v3 rollout that your team shipped earlier today.

Attached is a quick dashboard export (p95-dash-export.png) and a short sample of traces. User-visible errors are low, but latency is impacting the real-time quoting flow. Our business SLA requires <300ms p95.

Can Redwood:
- confirm if there was a variant or kernel change at that time,
- advise whether you can enable an automated fallback to m12q.v2 or an older runtime, and
- share expected impact on quality if you enable fallback (we can accept some accuracy loss for latency).

Time is sensitive — can we get a plan within the hour? If you need permission to flip traffic, consider this an explicit request to proceed with mitigations that reduce p95 even if they slightly reduce per-request score.

Thanks,
Alyssa Park
Head of Platform Ops, Finmetry
alyssa@finmetry.com

---
attachment: p95-dash-export.png (image/png)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa@finmetry.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p95 spike on m12q since 03:45 UTC — can you advise?

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the heads up and attaching the dashboard. We see the same signal on our side. Quick triage summary:

- Timeline: m12q.v3 deployed at 03:40 UTC (rolling kernel update + new compilation flags).
- Symptom: steep increase in KV-cache miss rate and longer kernel dispatch paths for longer sequences; aggregate p95 increased to ~600–900ms.
- Impact: user error rate remains low; quality of outputs appears unchanged for sampled prompts.

Mitigation options and tradeoffs:
1) Variant fallback to m12q.v2 (older weights/kernels) — expected p95 reduction to ~200–260ms, small drop in perplexity for a handful of prompts. Fast to flip and immediate.
2) Traffic split (30% to v2, 70% to v3) — gradual, allows us to monitor regression; less immediate relief for Finmetry.
3) Route Finmetry's traffic to your Dedicated pool (if configured) pinned to v2 runtime — preserves global rollout but requires your Dedicated config and may incur billing adjustments.
4) Roll forward with kernel revert and hotfix (slower; needs infra runbook & longer QA).

Request: we recommend enabling variant fallback for your tenant while we debug the kernel selection. We need explicit authorization to flip Finmetry to v2. If you approve, Rishi will perform the switch and we will preserve request traces and the model runtime profiles for root cause analysis.

I copied Naomi for any SLA/credits implications. Attaching kernel profiles and the tracer dump we captured (model12q-kernel-profiles.zip).

If we don’t hear back within 30 minutes we will proceed with an initial safe fallback for 50% of Finmetry traffic to reduce user impact (per our emergency playbook) — let me know if you prefer a different split.

- Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

attachment: model12q-kernel-profiles.zip (application/zip)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Park <alyssa@finmetry.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p95 spike on m12q since 03:45 UTC — decision and mitigation logistics

Thanks for the clear options, Priyom. From an account/SLA standpoint we should prioritize latency relief for Finmetry and avoid a customer-visible outage. I support immediate fallback to m12q.v2 for Finmetry with the following constraints:

- Preserve all request/response traces and kernel profiles for postmortem.
- Notify Finmetry of any estimated quality delta (we expect small regression on ~2% of edge prompts).
- Loop in Monica for any credits or contractual concessions if this persists >24 hours.
- Legal: keep a log of the change and timestamp for audit; we may need to reference it if Finmetry requests SLA relief.

Priyom/Rishi: you have authority to perform the fallback now. Please keep me posted with timestamps and the dashboard link.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa@finmetry.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: p95 spike on m12q — fallback activated and immediate outcomes

A quick operational update — performed the tenant-level fallback for Finmetry at 16:20 PDT (23:20 UTC). Details below and next steps.

What I did:
- Flipped Finmetry routing from m12q.v3 -> m12q.v2 for 100% of production requests via the safe-fallback API.
- Kept trace sampling at 100% for Finmetry and archived the kernel profile bundle (see attached).

Immediate outcome (observed on our dashboards):
- p95 for Finmetry dropped from ~610ms to ~210ms within two minutes.
- Error rate unchanged (very small fluctuations).
- Quality spot-check on sampled replies shows negligible regression for customer-critical prompts.

Next steps:
- Open JIRA INF-9482 for root cause analysis (kernel selection change + cache miss regression).
- Planned roll-forward: reproduce locally, apply targeted compilation flag revert, verify A/B against saved traces, then redeploy.
- If Finmetry prefers, we can keep v2 pinned until root cause is resolved; we will estimate TTR in 24 hours.

Alyssa — feel free to ping me if you want us to keep the fallback in place longer; Naomi / Monica will coordinate any SLA credit if this extends past the emergency window.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
